records.name: AssignmentOperationRecord

records.name: AssignmentProjection
records.role: durable assignment read projection with private CAS-preserved bounded recovery and Ready/terminal ACK receipts; receipts never appear in public Assignment JSON

replay_rules.rule: validate every operation record before applying it
order by last event sequence, recorded_at, then operation_id
dedupe events by task_id and sequence
keep same sequence events when task_id differs
sort task event histories by sequence
rebuild task current_assignment_id from newest assignment ordering
rebuild agent assignment lists in assignment creation order

For stable-key Ready and terminal events, atomically persist at most eight private hashed payload receipts with the operation and projection. Identical retries across replicas or restart restore the original event ACK and assignment acknowledgement fields without another event, outbox, log or span; reject semantic payload reuse and fail closed at the bound without evicting a receipt. A Ready ACK can authorize dispatch only while the current execution is still leased/ready with the same unexpired lease; Running, cancelling and terminal executions refuse it. The private receipt JSON is bounded to 16 KiB and validated before any durable write; the cap never evicts an original receipt.

Run selected fallback inventory authorization outside the assignment actor under caller cancellation and a two-second bound. The actor and each projection CAS retry recheck the observed assignment fingerprint, execution binding, active lease, state and request context; an intervening stop or lease/policy generation change invalidates approval.

Ready, recovery journal and terminal event persistence failures remain retryable: dependency unavailability or exhausted CAS returns 503, deadline 504 and cancellation 408 with fixed messages. Input validation stays 400. A daemon retries the same stable event key within its existing finite budget; storage failures never authorize dispatch. Legacy snapshot-only and write-only journal event paths mutate a private trial and publish or retain ACKs only after their single authority accepts persistence. A non-projection legacy journal combined with a snapshot store has no atomic receipt port and fails closed before either write; production projection-backed journals and local snapshot-only mode remain supported. Stale Ready/recovery lease rechecks have a two-second total lookup deadline, including operation-store actor queueing; timeout is retryable 504 and never publishes or caches an ACK. This bounds the existing background lookup but does not claim caller-context propagation through all actor operations.

Device-authenticated claims retain immutable device, owner-at-claim, assignment requester and hashed lease epoch in the same CAS transaction as lease/projection/journal writes. Replay and local snapshots retain this private claim across owner changes, stale scheduler repair and ordinary terminal events; legacy bearer claims have unknown provenance. The private observation reader returns blocked only for a current non-owner active lease and otherwise unknown, never permission. Confirmed execution termination, coverage/migration, installation linking and service-authenticated OAuth/API policy remain mandatory follow-up boundaries.

loop.observation: Stable event keys previously deduplicated only local event history and fallback inventory reads could occupy the global assignment actor after caller cancellation.
loop.hypothesis: Private bounded ACK receipts committed by projection CAS and cancellable candidate preflight outside the actor preserve retry identity and stop responsiveness across replicas.
loop.execute: Generate the reader doc and exercise replica/restart/CAS replay, changed-payload refusal, legacy repair preservation and cancellation/stop races before journal verification.
loop.evaluate: The journal verifier checks owning ports, source anchors and generated freshness; focused tests require exact original ACKs, no duplicate side effects and actor responsiveness during inventory stalls.
loop.retrospective: Ready and terminal ACK guarantees cover newly committed stable-key receipts; legacy records without receipts retain compatibility and cannot retroactively prove a lost original acknowledgement.
